name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q01 - Flame colours of alkali metals

questiontext.text:
Match the alkali metals in List I with the characteristic colours they impart to an oxidizing flame in List II:

List I (Alkali Metal)List II (Flame Colour)
(a) \(\mathrm{Li}\)(i) Blue
(b) \(\mathrm{Na}\)(ii) Yellow
(c) \(\mathrm{K}\)(iii) Crimson red
(d) \(\mathrm{Cs}\)(iv) Violet

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When alkali metals or their salts are heated in an oxidizing flame, the outermost valence electron is excited to a higher energy level. Upon returning to the ground state, radiation is emitted in the visible region of the spectrum.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Lithium (\(\mathrm{Li}\)) emits at \(\lambda = 670.8\text{ nm}\), imparting a crimson red colour. Sodium (\(\mathrm{Na}\)) emits at \(\lambda = 589.2\text{ nm}\), imparting a yellow colour. Potassium (\(\mathrm{K}\)) emits at \(\lambda = 766.5\text{ nm}\), imparting a violet colour. Caesium (\(\mathrm{Cs}\)) emits at \(\lambda = 455.5\text{ nm}\), imparting a blue colour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q02 - Flame colours of alkaline earth metals

questiontext.text:
Match the Group 2 elements in List I with their behaviour in a flame test in List II:

List I (Element)List II (Flame Colour)
(a) \(\mathrm{Be}\)(i) Apple green
(b) \(\mathrm{Ca}\)(ii) No colour
(c) \(\mathrm{Sr}\)(iii) Brick red
(d) \(\mathrm{Ba}\)(iv) Crimson

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Heavier alkaline earth metals undergo electronic excitation in a flame and emit visible light upon returning to the ground state, whereas beryllium and magnesium have valence electrons too strongly bound to be excited by flame energy.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Beryllium (\(\mathrm{Be}\)) imparts no colour to the flame. Calcium (\(\mathrm{Ca}\)) imparts a brick red colour. Strontium (\(\mathrm{Sr}\)) imparts a crimson colour. Barium (\(\mathrm{Ba}\)) imparts an apple green colour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q03 - Common names and formulas of sodium and calcium compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the common names of compounds in List I with their chemical formulas in List II:

List I (Common Name)List II (Chemical Formula)
(a) Washing soda(i) \(\mathrm{CaO}\)
(b) Baking soda(ii) \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\)
(c) Quick lime(iii) \(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\cdot\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
(d) Plaster of Paris(iv) \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\cdot 10\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrially important compounds of sodium and calcium are widely known by traditional names corresponding to specific hydration states or compositions.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\cdot 10\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\). Quick lime is calcium oxide, \(\mathrm{CaO}\). Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, \(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\cdot\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q04 - Products of alkali metals with oxygen and nitrogen

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions of alkali metals in List I with their major products in List II:

List I (Reaction)List II (Major Product)
(a) \(\mathrm{Li} + \text{excess }\mathrm{O}_2\)(i) \(\mathrm{KO}_2\) (superoxide)
(b) \(\mathrm{Na} + \text{excess }\mathrm{O}_2\)(ii) \(\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}\) (nitride)
(c) \(\mathrm{K} + \text{excess }\mathrm{O}_2\)(iii) \(\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}\) (monoxide)
(d) \(\mathrm{Li} + \mathrm{N}_2\text{ (air)}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) (peroxide)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
As the size of the alkali metal cation increases, larger anions such as peroxide (\(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\)) and superoxide (\(\mathrm{O}_2^-\)) are stabilised through lattice energy effects.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
On combustion in excess air/oxygen, lithium forms mainly the monoxide \(\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}\), sodium forms the peroxide \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2\), and potassium forms the superoxide \(\mathrm{KO}_2\). Additionally, lithium shows exceptional behaviour by reacting directly with nitrogen of air to form lithium nitride, \(\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q05 - Industrial uses of alkali metals and compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the alkali metal or compound in List I with its application in List II:

List I (Substance)List II (Application)
(a) Liquid \(\mathrm{Na}\) metal(i) Making armour plates
(b) \(\mathrm{Cs}\) metal(ii) Coolant in fast breeder nuclear reactors
(c) \(\mathrm{KOH}\)(iii) Devising photoelectric cells
(d) \(\mathrm{Li-Mg}\) alloy(iv) Absorbent of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and soft soap manufacture

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alkali metals and their hydroxides have specific industrial and technological uses based on their thermal, electrical, and chemical properties.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Liquid sodium metal is used as a coolant in fast breeder nuclear reactors. Caesium is used in devising photoelectric cells due to its low ionisation enthalpy. Potassium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{KOH}\)) is used in the manufacture of soft soap and as an excellent absorbent of carbon dioxide. Lithium is alloyed with magnesium to make armour plates.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q06 - Uses of alkaline earth metals and compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the alkaline earth metal or compound in List I with its use in List II:

List I (Substance)List II (Use)
(a) \(\mathrm{Cu-Be}\) alloy(i) Radiotherapy in cancer treatment
(b) Metallic \(\mathrm{Be}\)(ii) Windows of X-ray tubes
(c) Suspension of \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)}_2\) in water(iii) High strength springs
(d) Radium salts(iv) Antacid in medicine

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Group 2 elements and their compounds find applications across metallurgy, medical imaging, pharmaceuticals, and oncology.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Copper-beryllium alloys are used to prepare high strength springs. Metallic beryllium is used for making windows of X-ray tubes. An aqueous suspension of magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is used as an antacid in medicine. Radium salts are used in radiotherapy for cancer treatment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q07 - Biological significance of s-block ions

questiontext.text:
Match the biologically important ions in List I with their primary biological role or location in List II:

List I (Ion)List II (Biological Role / Location)
(a) \(\mathrm{Na}^+\)(i) Cofactor for ATP-utilising phosphate transfer enzymes; present in chlorophyll
(b) \(\mathrm{K}^+\)(ii) Most abundant cation within cell fluids; participates in glucose oxidation to produce ATP
(c) \(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\)(iii) Found primarily outside cells in blood plasma; transports sugars and amino acids into cells
(d) \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\)(iv) \(99\%\) present in bones and teeth; involved in blood coagulation

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Monovalent \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and \(\mathrm{K}^+\) and divalent \(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) perform distinct, essential physiological functions across cellular compartments.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Sodium ions (\(\mathrm{Na}^+\)) are primarily extracellular (in blood plasma and interstitial fluid) and participate in transporting sugars and amino acids into cells. Potassium ions (\(\mathrm{K}^+\)) are the most abundant cations inside cell fluids, where they activate enzymes and participate in glucose oxidation to ATP. Magnesium ions (\(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\)) act as cofactors for all enzymes utilising ATP in phosphate transfer and are present in chlorophyll. About \(99\%\) of body calcium (\(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\)) is in bones and teeth, and it also plays a vital role in blood coagulation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q08 - Hydration of Group 1 and Group 2 chlorides

questiontext.text:
Match the metal chlorides in List I with the form in which they crystallise from aqueous solution in List II:

List I (Chloride)List II (Crystalline Form)
(a) \(\mathrm{LiCl}\)(i) \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{CaCl}_2\)(ii) Anhydrous (does not form hydrate)
(c) \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\)(iii) \(\mathrm{LiCl}\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{NaCl}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{CaCl}_2\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The tendency to form hydrated halides depends on the hydration enthalpy of the cation, which increases with higher charge and smaller ionic radius.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Among alkali metal chlorides, \(\mathrm{LiCl}\) crystallises as the dihydrate \(\mathrm{LiCl}\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) due to the high hydration enthalpy of \(\mathrm{Li}^+\), whereas \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) does not form hydrates. Among alkaline earth metal chlorides, the tendency to form hydrates decreases down the group: \(\mathrm{CaCl}_2\) crystallises as \(\mathrm{CaCl}_2\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), while \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\) crystallises as \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q09 - Hydrolysis reactions of alkali metals and oxides

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions with water in List I with the products formed in List II (where \(\mathrm{M}\) is an alkali metal):

List I (Reactants)List II (Products)
(a) \(\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(i) \(\mathrm{M}^+ + \mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\)
(b) \(\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{M}^+ + \mathrm{OH}^-\) only
(c) \(\mathrm{MO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{M}^+ + \mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\)
(d) \(\mathrm{M} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{M}^+ + \mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alkali metals and their oxides, peroxides, and superoxides react vigorously with water to yield alkaline hydroxide solutions, with additional redox products depending on the oxidation state of oxygen or the metal.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
The monoxide reacts as \(\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{M}^+ + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\) (hydroxide only). The peroxide reacts as \(\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{M}^+ + 2\mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\). The superoxide reacts as \(2\mathrm{MO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{M}^+ + 2\mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\). The free metal reacts as \(2\mathrm{M} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{M}^+ + 2\mathrm{OH}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q10 - Average oxide composition of Portland cement

questiontext.text:
Match the oxide constituents of Portland cement in List I with their average percentage composition in List II:

List I (Oxide)List II (Average Composition)
(a) \(\mathrm{CaO}\)(i) \(5\text{--}10\%\)
(b) \(\mathrm{SiO}_2\)(ii) \(2\text{--}3\%\)
(c) \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)(iii) \(50\text{--}60\%\)
(d) \(\mathrm{MgO}\)(iv) \(20\text{--}25\%\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Portland cement is manufactured by fusing lime-rich material (\(\mathrm{CaO}\)) with clay containing silica (\(\mathrm{SiO}_2\)) and oxides of aluminium, iron, and magnesium.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
The average oxide composition of Portland cement is: \(\mathrm{CaO}\) \(50\text{--}60\%\), \(\mathrm{SiO}_2\) \(20\text{--}25\%\), \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) \(5\text{--}10\%\), and \(\mathrm{MgO}\) \(2\text{--}3\%\) (with \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) \(1\text{--}2\%\) and \(\mathrm{SO}_3\) \(1\text{--}2\%\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q11 - Ingredients of Portland cement and their proportions

questiontext.text:
Match the important ingredients present in Portland cement in List I with their percentage by weight in List II:

List I (Ingredient)List II (Percentage)
(a) Tricalcium silicate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_3\mathrm{SiO}_5\))(i) \(11\%\)
(b) Dicalcium silicate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_2\mathrm{SiO}_4\))(ii) \(2\text{--}3\%\)
(c) Tricalcium aluminate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_3\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_6\))(iii) \(51\%\)
(d) Gypsum (\(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\))(iv) \(26\%\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Portland cement is obtained by mixing cement clinker (formed from limestone and clay) with a small amount of gypsum to slow down the setting process.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
The important ingredients present in Portland cement are tricalcium silicate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_3\mathrm{SiO}_5\)) at \(51\%\), dicalcium silicate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_2\mathrm{SiO}_4\)) at \(26\%\), and tricalcium aluminate (\(\mathrm{Ca}_3\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_6\)) at \(11\%\), while \(2\text{--}3\%\) by weight of gypsum (\(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)) is added to the clinker.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q12 - Industrial processes for sodium and calcium compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial processes or conditions in List I with the corresponding products or intermediates in List II:

List I (Process / Condition)List II (Product / Intermediate)
(a) Solvay process(i) Dead burnt plaster (\(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\))
(b) Castner-Kellner cell(ii) Quick lime (\(\mathrm{CaO}\)) from limestone
(c) Heating \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3\) in a rotary kiln at \(1070\text{--}1270\text{ K}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) via sodium amalgam
(d) Heating gypsum above \(393\text{ K}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\) via \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\) precipitation

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Large-scale manufacture of sodium and calcium compounds relies on specific electrolytic, precipitation, and thermal decomposition processes.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
The Solvay process produces sodium carbonate (\(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\)) by precipitating \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\) and heating it. The Castner-Kellner cell electrolyses brine using a mercury cathode to form sodium amalgam, which reacts with water to give \(\mathrm{NaOH}\). Heating limestone (\(\mathrm{CaCO}_3\)) in a rotary kiln at \(1070\text{--}1270\text{ K}\) produces quick lime (\(\mathrm{CaO}\)). Heating gypsum above \(393\text{ K}\) removes all water of crystallisation to yield anhydrous \(\mathrm{CaSO}_4\) (dead burnt plaster).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q13 - Standard electrode potentials of s-block elements

questiontext.text:
Match the redox couples in List I with their standard electrode potentials (\(E^\circ\)) in List II:

List I (Redox Couple)List II (\(E^\circ / \text{V}\))
(a) \(\mathrm{Li}^+ / \mathrm{Li}\)(i) \(-1.97\text{ V}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{Na}^+ / \mathrm{Na}\)(ii) \(-3.04\text{ V}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+} / \mathrm{Be}\)(iii) \(-2.92\text{ V}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+} / \mathrm{Ba}\)(iv) \(-2.714\text{ V}\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standard reduction potentials (\(E^\circ\)) reflect the combined effect of sublimation/atomisation enthalpy, ionisation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy. Alkali metals are stronger reducing agents than alkaline earth metals, with \(\mathrm{Li}\) being the strongest reducing agent overall and \(\mathrm{Be}\) having the least negative \(E^\circ\) among Group 2 metals.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
For \(\mathrm{Li}^+/\mathrm{Li}\), \(E^\circ = -3.04\text{ V}\) (most negative). For \(\mathrm{Na}^+/\mathrm{Na}\), \(E^\circ = -2.714\text{ V}\) (least negative among Group 1). For \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+}/\mathrm{Be}\), \(E^\circ = -1.97\text{ V}\) (least negative among Group 2). For \(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}/\mathrm{Ba}\), \(E^\circ = -2.92\text{ V}\) (most negative among Group 2).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q14 - Thermal decomposition of nitrates and carbonates

questiontext.text:
Match the salts heated in List I with the products obtained upon thermal decomposition in List II:

List I (Salt)List II (Decomposition Products)
(a) \(\mathrm{NaNO}_3\)(i) \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\)
(b) \(\mathrm{LiNO}_3\)(ii) \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3 + \mathrm{CO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3\) (at \(1200\text{ K}\))(iii) \(\mathrm{NaNO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\)
(d) \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\)(iv) \(\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\)

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thermal decomposition pathways of oxo-salts depend on the polarising power of the cation and the stability of the resulting oxide or nitrite.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Sodium nitrate decomposes to sodium nitrite and oxygen: \(2\mathrm{NaNO}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaNO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\). Lithium nitrate behaves anomalously (like Group 2 nitrates) to give the oxide: \(4\mathrm{LiNO}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O} + 4\mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2\). Calcium carbonate decomposes at \(1200\text{ K}\) as \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\). Sodium hydrogencarbonate decomposes on heating as \(2\mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3 + \mathrm{CO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q15 - Solubility trends and enthalpy explanations

questiontext.text:
Match the aqueous solubility observations in List I with their correct thermodynamic explanations in List II:

List I (Observation)List II (Explanation)
(a) Low solubility of \(\mathrm{LiF}\) in water(i) Lattice enthalpy stays nearly constant while hydration enthalpy decreases down the group
(b) Low solubility of \(\mathrm{CsI}\) in water(ii) Smaller hydration enthalpy of its two large ions
(c) Solubility of \(\mathrm{M(OH)}_2\) increases down Group 2(iii) Lattice enthalpy decreases much more than hydration enthalpy down the group
(d) Solubility of \(\mathrm{MSO}_4\) decreases down Group 2(iv) Very high lattice enthalpy

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aqueous solubility of ionic solids is governed by the relative magnitudes of lattice enthalpy and hydration enthalpy.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
\(\mathrm{LiF}\) has low solubility in water due to its very high lattice enthalpy (small \(\mathrm{Li}^+\) and \(\mathrm{F}^-\) ions). \(\mathrm{CsI}\) has low solubility in water due to the smaller hydration enthalpy of its two large ions. For Group 2 hydroxides (\(\mathrm{M(OH)}_2\)), lattice enthalpy decreases much more than hydration enthalpy as cationic radius increases down the group, so solubility increases. For Group 2 sulphates (\(\mathrm{MSO}_4\)), the large \(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\) anion keeps lattice enthalpy nearly constant while hydration enthalpy decreases down the group, so solubility decreases.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q16 - Diagonal relationship properties of Li-Mg and Be-Al

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical species or reactions in List I with their characteristic diagonal-relationship features in List II:

List I (Species / Reaction)List II (Feature)
(a) \(\mathrm{Be(OH)}_2\) in excess alkali(i) Strong tendency to form fluoro complexes \(\mathrm{BeF}_4^{2-}\) and \(\mathrm{AlF}_6^{3-}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{BeCl}_2\) and \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\) in vapour phase(ii) Direct combination forms nitrides \(\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}_3\mathrm{N}_2\)
(c) \(\mathrm{Li}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\) with nitrogen(iii) Dissolves to form beryllate ion \([\mathrm{Be(OH)}_4]^{2-}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Al}^{3+}\) with fluoride(iv) \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)-bridged structure; strong Lewis acids

Choose the correct match from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diagonal relationships between \(\mathrm{Li}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\), and between \(\mathrm{Be}\) and \(\mathrm{Al}\), arise from similarities in ionic sizes and/or charge-to-radius ratios.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Beryllium hydroxide dissolves in excess alkali to give the beryllate ion \([\mathrm{Be(OH)}_4]^{2-}\), just as \(\mathrm{Al(OH)}_3\) gives \([\mathrm{Al(OH)}_4]^-\). Both \(\mathrm{BeCl}_2\) and \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\) have \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)-bridged structures in the vapour phase, are soluble in organic solvents, and act as strong Lewis acids. Both \(\mathrm{Li}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\) react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides (\(\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}_3\mathrm{N}_2\)). Both \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Al}^{3+}\) have a strong tendency to form complexes such as \(\mathrm{BeF}_4^{2-}\) and \(\mathrm{AlF}_6^{3-}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).
